title: Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Downtown Line construction cost
sections.summary: The Downtown Line cost $21 billion, close to 5% of GDP in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, the construction of the Downtown Line cost $21 billion, or close to 5% of our gross domestic product (GDP) in 2017.

sections.label: Rail Infrastructure Fund announcement
sections.summary: The Government announced the Rail Infrastructure Fund at Budget 2018 to set aside funds for the rail network.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We should be responsible and set aside funds to invest in our rail network for the benefit of future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This is why the Government announced the Rail Infrastructure Fund (RIF) earlier this year at Budget 2018.

sections.label: LTA Amendment Bill proposal
sections.summary: MOT proposes the LTA (Amendment) Bill to formalise the establishment of the RIF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In line with this, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) proposes to enact the Land Transport Authority (LTA) (Amendment) Bill to formalise the establishment of the RIF.

sections.label: RIF and RSF funding sources
sections.summary: The RIF is made up solely of Government subsidies, while the RSF mixes Government subsidies and Licence Charge from rail operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: While the RIF is solely made up of Government subsidies, the RSF comprises a mix of Government subsidies and Licence Charge collected from the rail operators under the New Rail Financing Framework.

sections.label: Rail ridership and asset transfer
sections.summary: LTA 2017 statistics show average combined daily MRT and LRT ridership of about 3.3 million, and since 2016 operators have transferred rail assets to the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on statistics released by LTA in 2017, the average combined daily ridership on our rail MRT and LRT networks is approximately 3.3 million per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Since 2016, train operators have gradually transferred their rail assets to the Government under the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF).

sections.label: 2017 train disruptions
sections.summary: Several high-profile train disruptions occurred in 2017, including the Bishan tunnel flooding and the Joo Koon collision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, there have been several high-profile train disruptions in 2017, such as the flooding of the MRT tunnel in Bishan, the Joo Koon train collision, and a series of incidents that affected three train lines on the same day in November 2017.

sections.label: NRFF licence charge and RIF
sections.summary: The NRFF introduced a licence charge paid by train operators into an RSF, and the 2018 Budget announced a $5 billion injection into the RIF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The NRFF also introduced a new framework to enhance the financial sustainability of the network – train operators will now pay a licence charge into an RSF that can be used to build, replace or upgrade operating assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was subsequently announced in the 2018 Budget that the Government will inject $5 billion into the RIF that the Minister spoke on earlier.

sections.label: Minister on rail line costs
sections.summary: In a 13 November 2017 speech, the Minister for Transport said the North-South Line costs about $160 million per km and the Downtown Line about $490 million per km.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a speech that the Minister for Transport gave on 13 November 2017, he noted that the North-South Line costs about $160 million per kilometre (km), while the Downtown Line costs about $490 million per km to build.

sections.label: SMRT engineering staff target
sections.summary: In 2017, SMRT announced it was on track to increase its engineering staff strength to 700 engineers by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2017, SMRT announced that they were on track to increase their engineering staff strength to 700 engineers by 2020.

sections.label: SMRT trains FY2018 loss
sections.summary: SMRT trains lost $86 million in FY2018 because fare revenue does not match the operating expenditure needed for a high-quality, reliable system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMRT trains lost $86 million in the financial year (FY) 2018 because fare revenue simply does not match the operating expenditure required to provide a high-quality, reliable system.

sections.label: Contracting model for rail sector
sections.summary: A similar contracting model that mitigates fare revenue risks and gets value for money through competition or benchmarking may be needed for rail.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A similar contracting model that mitigates fare revenue risks for rail operators, that also gets value for money through competition or benchmarking, may be needed for the rail sector.

sections.label: Rail renewal and fare study
sections.summary: The Minister for Transport said $4 billion will be spent renewing the rail system over five years, and an NTU study found our fares were second lowest among 12 major cities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For rail, the Minister for Transport said in the Committee of Supply debate this year that $4 billion will be spent to renew the rail system over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, a Nanyang Technological University (NTU) study, commissioned by the Public Transport Council, found that our fares were the second lowest among 12 major cities worldwide.

sections.label: Network Capacity Factor fares
sections.summary: The Public Transport Council introduced the Network Capacity Factor, linking fares to relative supply and demand for public transport services, called a good first step.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Public Transport Council’s introduction of the Network Capacity Factor, which links fares to the relative supply and demand for public transport services, is a good first step.

sections.label: Government public engagement transport funding
sections.summary: The Government has to do more to engage the public, placing it on a firm financial footing to continue providing a world-class public transport system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, the Government has to do more to engage the public to discover this.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It places the Government on a firm financial footing to continue to provide a world-class public transport system.

sections.label: Resignalling project line reliability
sections.summary: After the resignalling project was completed, the reliability of the line has improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After the completion of the resignalling project, the reliability of the line has improved.

sections.label: Citizens knowing true service cost
sections.summary: Spending depends on citizens' needs and expectations, so citizens need to know the true cost of service provision, while fares after subsidies remain affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the long run, our spending depends on our citizens' needs and expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, our citizens need to know the true cost of service provision, even though we continue to ensure that fares, after subsidies, remain affordable to the broader public.

sections.label: Communicating MRT true cost
sections.summary: Through various channels, including MRT station platforms and trains, the true cost of MRT networks per trip should be communicated to people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, from time to time, through various channels, including on the MRT station platforms and trains, we should communicate to our people the true cost of our MRT networks per trip.

sections.label: LTA charging RSF RIF expenses
sections.summary: The question asks how LTA will ensure expenses are charged accurately in the RSF and/or RIF, since demolition and replacement expenses could be for both funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In clause 6(a), can I check how LTA will ensure that the expenses are charged accurately in the RSF and/or RIF since "demolition and replacement" expenses could be for both funds?

sections.label: Government bus and rail subsidies
sections.summary: Over five years, the Government is subsidising $5 billion for buses, $4 billion for rail asset renewal and $20 billion for rail infrastructure expansion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Over the next five years, the Government is subsidising $5 billion for bus services, $4 billion for renewal of rail operating assets and $20 billion to expand our rail infrastructure.

sections.label: RSF funding restriction
sections.summary: Section 13A of the LTA of Singapore Act does not permit the RSF to fund demolition and replacement of rail infrastructure such as tracks and tunnels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The RSF is not permitted by section 13A of the LTA of Singapore Act to fund the "demolition and replacement" of rail infrastructure, such as tracks and tunnels.

sections.label: Rail manpower development fund
sections.summary: To attract, develop and retain skilled engineers and technicians, the rail engineering vocation is being professionalised and a $12.5 million Public Transport Manpower Development Fund seeded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To attract, develop and retain skilled engineers and technicians for the land transport sector, we are professionalising the rail engineering vocation and have seeded a $12.5 million Public Transport Manpower Development Fund to drive manpower development initiatives.

sections.label: MRT reliability MKBF increase
sections.summary: MRT Mean Kilometres Between Failure was 181,000 train-km last year and tripled to 661,000 train-km for the first three quarters of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Last year, the Mean Kilometres Between Failure (MKBF) for our MRT network was 181,000 train-km.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This has tripled to 661,000 train-km for the first three quarters of this year.

sections.label: Minister's rail reliability target
sections.summary: The Minister for Transport set an objective target of one million MKBF for the MRT network by 2020, to be sustained thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Instead of a complex expenditure-performance ratio, the Minister for Transport has laid out a very clear objective target for rail reliability – to achieve one million MKBF for the MRT network by 2020 and sustain it at that level going forward.

sections.label: New Rail Financing Framework transition
sections.summary: LTA has just completed transitioning all rail lines to the New Rail Financing Framework this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: LTA has just completed transitioning all rail lines to the New Rail Financing Framework this year.

sections.label: 1982 MRT lines commitment
sections.summary: After 15 years of study, the Government committed in 1982 to build the N-S and E-W Lines for $5 billion, close to 15% of GDP then.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: After 15 years of careful study, the Government committed in 1982 to build the N-S and E-W Lines at a price of $5 billion, close to 15% of Singapore’s GDP at the time.

sections.label: Eight MRT lines by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, adding the Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line will bring the total to eight MRT lines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: By 2030, with the addition of the Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line, we will have a total of eight MRT lines.
